### Overall team records
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=UEFA_European_Championship_records_and_statistics&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Overall team records")]
The system used in the European Championship up to 1992 was 2 points for a win, and [3 points for a win](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_points_for_a_win "Three points for a win") from 1996 onwards. In this ranking 3 points are awarded for a win, 1 for a draw and 0 for a loss. As per statistical convention in football, matches decided in [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_\(sports\)#Association_football "Overtime \(sports\)") are counted as wins and losses, while matches decided by [penalty shoot-outs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_\(association_football\) "Penalty shoot-out \(association football\)") are counted as draws. Teams are ranked by total points, then by goal difference, then by goals scored.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship_records_and_statistics#cite_note-6)     _As of[UEFA Euro 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2024 "UEFA Euro 2024")_

### Hosts
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=UEFA_European_Championship_records_and_statistics&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Hosts")]
From [1960](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_European_Nations'_Cup "1960 European Nations' Cup") to [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_1976 "UEFA Euro 1976") the host was decided between one of the four semi-finalists. Since [1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_1980 "UEFA Euro 1980") the hosts have automatically qualified, except in [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2020 "UEFA Euro 2020") when every country had to qualify through qualification. Germany has hosted the finals in [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2024 "UEFA Euro 2024").

### Countries that have never qualified
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=UEFA_European_Championship_records_and_statistics&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Countries that have never qualified")]
See also: [UEFA European Championship qualifying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship_qualifying "UEFA European Championship qualifying")
The following teams are current or former UEFA members which have never qualified for the European Championship. Of these, Bosnia and Herzegovina ([2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup"), [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup "2026 FIFA World Cup")) and Israel ([1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_FIFA_World_Cup "1970 FIFA World Cup")) are the only teams to qualify for the [FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup"), though Israel did so as an [Asian Football Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Football_Confederation "Asian Football Confederation") (AFC) member.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship_records_and_statistics#cite_note-:0-22) [Saarland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saarland_national_football_team "Saarland national football team") didn't exist by 1960 when the European Championship was introduced and East Germany, that qualified to the FIFA World Cup in [1974](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_FIFA_World_Cup "1974 FIFA World Cup"), never qualified for the European Championship until it ceased to exist in 1990.
**Legend**
  * •  – Did not qualify
  * ×  – Did not enter / Withdrew / Banned
